title: Daily Output Almanac (Hexad) — Juno Li
content:
Purpose: quick, low-friction daily ledger for tracking six tiny signals (the hexad) that map to my weekly KPI targets. This is intentionally terse: jot, triage, act. Not a polished report — scratchpad style.

How I use it (workflow):
- Morning: capture intention for the day (one-line).
- Midday: quick pulse check (1–2 bullets).
- End of day: add counts, one insight, one tiny experiment to try tomorrow.
- Weekly: roll up hexad totals into a simple progress score and decide 1 change.

Hexad signals (short names):
1) Reach — outbound devs contacted (calls/DMs).
2) Demos — product demo or prototype time (minutes).
3) Tokens — focused writing output (approx 300-token units; rough).
4) Tests — short micro-evals or smoke tests run.
5) Syncs — synchronous meetings that advanced work (count).
6) Recovery — time spent on sleep/exercise/mental reset (minutes).

Target KPIs (weekly):
- Reach >= 8 (people)
- Demos >= 2 sessions or 240 minutes total
- Tokens >= 20 units (~6000 tokens total)
- Tests >= 6 micro-evals
- Syncs <= 6 (avoid meeting bloat) but those should be high signal
- Recovery >= 210 minutes (30 min/day avg)

Scoring heuristic (quick):
- For each signal, assign 0/0.5/1 depending on meeting threshold. Sum gives weekly score out of 6. If >=4.5 consider week "green."

Notes on metrics:
- Tokens are awkward to estimate in daily life; I count 300-token blobs as one "unit". Anything less than ~150 tokens is "half". This keeps the counting lightweight.
- Tests include quick ablation runs, unit prompts, smoke comparisons. Not full evals.

Today (2025-01-10) — End-of-day entry:
- Intention (AM): finish prototype for low-latency cache demo; capture timings.
- Midday pulse: prototype integrates but KV cache propagation delayed; switch to smaller batch size.
- Outcome metrics: Reach=2 (DM convo + quick sync), Demos=1 (90m), Tokens=3.5, Tests=2, Syncs=1, Recovery=25m.
- Insight: switching to smaller batch lowered tail latency but increased token cost; need to test prefix caching which may give both latency and cost wins.
- Micro-experiment for tomorrow: add a 3-key prefix cache layer and run 6 quick traces (GHA job) in the morning.
- Quick TODOs: open JIRA-PI-4567 to log latency-change experiment results; ping infra about kernel-selection logs.

Weekly rollup (week ending 2025-01-10):
- Totals: Reach=9, Demos=3, Tokens=22, Tests=7, Syncs=5, Recovery=180m
- Score calc: Reach(1)+Demos(1)+Tokens(1)+Tests(1)+Syncs(1)+Recovery(0.5) = 5.5/6 -> green but recovery low.
- Reflection: shipping velocity was high; mental energy dropped midweek. Recovery needs a hard constraint (no meetings after 4pm Wed/Thu).

Hypotheses to test next week: 
H1: Enabling 3-key prefix cache + batch size 4 will reduce p95 latency by >=12% while keeping cost < +5%. (Action: run 6 traces across 3 workloads, tag with GITHUB-issue-223)
H2: Consolidating two demos into one 2-hour block reduces context-switch overhead and increases tokens-per-hour by >=15%. (Action: block two demo-hours into one slot)

Experiments matrix (quick):
- Experiment A (prefix-cache): metric=p95 latency, secondary=token-cost; run size=6 traces; owner=me
- Experiment B (demo-blocking): metric=tokens/hour; run size=3 weeks; owner=me

Retro notes (short):
- Wins: prototype reached demoable quality; quick smoke tests caught a bad kv-eviction bug early.
- Frictions: meeting drift on Wed wasted 45m; had to shift focus late.
- Decisions: enforce gentle meeting guardrails next week; try EOD priority list (3 items).

Template for daily entry (keep under 6 lines):
- AM intention: [one line]
- Midday: [one short note]
- Metrics: R/X, D/X, T/X, S/X, SYNC/X, REC/X
- EOD insight: [one line]
- Tomorrow micro-experiment: [one line]

Signals I ignore here (deliberate): code review counts, deep research minutes, email triage. Those live in separate trackers — this ledger prioritizes outward movement (reach/demo) and measurable output.

Housekeeping:
- Link raw traces to GITHUB-issue-223 as they complete.
- If prefix-cache shows >10% p95 regression, escalate to infra channel and drop experiment.

Open questions (for future clarification):
- Is my recovery target realistic during heavy sprint weeks? Maybe scale to 180 min per week during ship sprints.
- Should "tests" include cross-team evals? For now keep it local to quick technical checks.

Random scribbles (brainstorm hooks):
- Micro-review ritual: 3-min read of last 3 demos before starting a new one. Could improve demo prep.
- Visual weekly mosaic: quick 6-box heatmap (signal x day) on Friday to spot patterns.

Footer: quick tag lines to myself — "ship small, measure twice, rest before focus."

(End of entry)
